struck: The typical monthly HOA fee on a condo for sale in the nine areas is $609.
use: The typical HOA fee shown on a condominium listed in these areas is about $650 a month.

pattern: \bmost are in the (?:MLS )?areas along the ocean
struck: In North Myrtle Beach, Myrtle Beach and Surfside Beach most are in the MLS areas along the ocean.
use: Most homes for sale with no HOA fee are listed as not in a named subdivision.

struck: Listing remarks in Ocean Lakes say each home is on leased land with a yearly lease paid twice a year.
use: A listing with no HOA fee can still carry a yearly charge: 15 of 82 no-fee listings in campground communities say in their remarks that the home is on leased land.

struck: A seller's disclosure statement must cover whether the home is governed by an HOA.
use: For most sales, a seller must give the buyer a written disclosure statement that asks whether the property is subject to governance of a homeowners association.

pattern: \bcounty does not pick up trash|\blists private haulers
struck: Outside city and town limits, the county does not pick up trash at the curb. The county authority lists private haulers that offer trash and recycling service there.
use: The Horry County Solid Waste Authority does not provide curbside trash or recycling pickup.

pattern: stormwater fee[^.]{0,100}\bHOA or not|\bpay the same flat fee
struck: Every home in unincorporated Horry County pays a county stormwater fee on its property tax bill, HOA or not. Townhomes and condos pay the same flat fee.
use: Property owners in unincorporated Horry County pay a county stormwater fee on the property tax bill. Townhomes and condominiums pay a flat fee, amount not shown.

pattern: Back yard, not near the lot lines|\bR-1 and R-2\b
struck: Back yard, not near the lot lines. In the R-1 and R-2 districts, a home may have one work vehicle of no more than 2 tons.
use: In the R-1.4, R-1.5, R-1.7 and R-2 districts a home may have one commercial, industrial, farm or construction vehicle of no more than 2 tons.

struck: The county's zoning sets no limit on where an owner parks his own boat, trailer, camper or work truck on a home lot.
use: Outside the towns, Horry County sets no rule on where on a residential lot you park your own boat, boat trailer or camper.

struck: A lawyer runs every home closing.
use: A home closing is done under the supervision of a lawyer.

struck: The county asks pond owners to inspect twice a year, to keep the pond holding water.
use: The inspections help keep storage capacity, stop erosion and control algae.

struck: The county never maintains a private road.
use: The county maintains the roads it owns.

struck: The county's online GIS map, linked from its Land Info page, shows each parcel; its map service carries a layer of the town limits.
use: The county's Map Your Move map, linked from its Land Info page, shows the municipality for a parcel.

pattern: \ba fifth of an acre|\bthree[- ]quarters of an acre
struck: North Myrtle Beach a fifth of an acre; Loris three quarters of an acre.
use: About 0.7 in Loris and 0.16 in North Myrtle Beach.

struck: Myrtle Beach a third of an acre.
use: On a little over a third of an acre.

pattern: \b(?:most|they|houses) (?:sit|stand) on (?:their|its) own lot|\bown lot along a country road
struck: So most sit on their own lot along a country road.
use: Almost none are listed in a subdivision.

struck: The biggest houses of the eight areas.
use: The middle house is about 2,400 square feet, the largest middle size of the eight areas.

pattern: Huntington Beach State Park[^.]{0,60}\b15 minutes|\b15 minutes[^.]{0,60}Huntington Beach State Park
struck: About 15 minutes from Murrells Inlet to Huntington Beach State Park.
use: About 10 minutes from Murrells Inlet to Huntington Beach State Park, with no traffic.

pattern: \bsome of its streets are on canals|\bcanals that run to the marsh
struck: So some of its streets are on canals that run to the marsh.
use: Cherry Grove has canals, and about 415 properties pay the city a yearly fee to dredge them.

struck: Lakeside Crossing
use: (Do not name Lakeside Crossing: its blank fee is a land lease and an association.)

struck: Some are on older streets in central Conway, such as Temple Street and Cherry Street.
use: Some are on streets in central Conway, such as Temple Street and Cherry Street.

struck: In Socastee, they were in Rosewood Estates and Bridge Creek, built in the 1980s.
use: In Socastee, they were in Rosewood Estates and Bridge Creek, built from 1979 to 1988.

struck: The house has no HOA.
use: The house is listed with no HOA fee.

pattern: \bolder house in Cherry Grove, Windy Hill or Ocean Drive|\b1976 to 1981
struck: In North Myrtle Beach, an older house in Cherry Grove, Windy Hill or Ocean Drive. Coastal Heights houses built 1976 to 1981.
use: In North Myrtle Beach, this band buys a house in Cherry Grove, Windy Hill or Ocean Drive; in Cherry Grove nearly all were built before 1990.

pattern: \bThey line Ocean Boulevard|\bOthers are in older neighborhoods
struck: They line Ocean Boulevard in Myrtle Beach and North Myrtle Beach and South Waccamaw Drive. Others are in older neighborhoods.
use: Some are on Ocean Boulevard in Myrtle Beach and North Myrtle Beach and on South Waccamaw Drive in Garden City. Others were listed with no fee in Pine Lakes and Plantation Point.

struck: The owners along them pay the city a yearly fee to dredge them.
use: Owners of about 400 properties in the canal district pay the city a yearly fee to dredge them.

struck: Surfside Beach was a rice plantation called The Ark, then Floral Beach.
use: The land was part of a rice plantation called The Ark and was later named Floral Beach.

struck: Murrells Inlet takes its name from John Morrall.
use: Maps from the early 1800s call the inlet Murray's Inlet or Morrall's, the second after John Morrall, who bought 610 acres on the inlet in 1731.

struck: Its seafood restaurants grew from the oyster roasts and fried shore dinners of its founding families. The MarshWalk links a row of them.
use: People first came to the inlet for oyster roasts and fried shore dinners, and seafood restaurants followed.

struck: Conway began as Kingston, on a bluff of the Waccamaw River.
use: Conway began in the 1730s as Kingston Village, on a bluff of the Waccamaw River.

pattern: \bbuilt the Ocean Forest Hotel|\bfirst owners sold
struck: In the 1920s the Woodside family built the Ocean Forest Hotel and the Pine Lakes golf course. Its first owners sold oceanfront lots for $25 each.
use: The Woodside family bought land in the 1920s and finished the Pine Lakes golf course and the Ocean Forest Hotel just before the Great Depression. In 1901 the railroad company began selling oceanfront lots for $25 each.

struck: Coastal Grand, the nearest big mall, is about 50 minutes away.
use: Coastal Grand Mall in Myrtle Beach is a drive of about 50 minutes from the center of Loris, with no traffic.

pattern: \bshort walk\b|\bclose enough to walk\b|\bwalk to the (?:beach|sand)
struck: Most of them a short walk from the sand. None of the houses for sale here is close enough to walk to the beach.
use: Most are within half a mile of the ocean shore. None of the houses for sale in Little River is within a mile of the beach.

struck: Galivants Ferry is also home to the Galivants Ferry Stump Meeting, a Democratic Party tradition.
use: (Dropped by the coordinator: a party-political event.)

struck: The Bog-Off features a parade, crafts, bands and fireworks.
use: The Bog-Off brings vendors, a car show and two stages of live music.

struck: On the south side of the city, Myrtle Beach State Park opened in 1936 as the first park in South Carolina's state park system.
use: Myrtle Beach State Park opened in 1936 as the first of South Carolina's state parks to open.

struck: A piece of the old road is still at its front.
use: A small piece of the original Kings Highway, a colonial route between Boston and Charleston, is still at its front.

pattern: \bdug through the marsh|\bat any tide|\bdredged them twice|\bfilling with silt
struck: Cherry Grove's canals were dug through the marsh in the 1950s and 1960s. By the 1970s, some were filling with silt. The city has dredged them twice, so boats can reach House Creek and the Intracoastal Waterway at any tide.
use: Cherry Grove's canals were created as early as the 1950s. By the 1970s, some were filling up. The city has dredged canals there twice since 2016, to give owners boat access to House Creek and the Intracoastal Waterway at high and low tide.

struck: Owners pay the city about $1,700 a year for that work, on the tax bill.
use: Owners of about 415 properties in the canal district pay the city about $1,700 a year for that work, on the county tax bill.

pattern: \bIn those years it was also a farm center
struck: In those years it was also a farm center for the country around it.
use: In the late 1800s it was also a farm center for the country around it.

struck: Inlet captains have long taken visiting anglers offshore on charter and party trips.
use: In the twentieth century a fleet of charter and party boats grew up at the inlet, and its captains took visiting anglers offshore.

pattern: \bIn our experience, many HOAs here do not allow renting
struck: No HOA rule against renting the home out. In our experience, many HOAs here do not allow renting a house out at all.
use: No HOA rule against renting the home out.

struck: Many of the houses listed with no fee are on the ocean side of US 17 Business, the coast road, and houses there cost more.
use: About a third of the houses listed with no fee are on the ocean side of US 17 Business, and they list at about $800,000, against about $435,000 for the others.

pattern: Myrtle Heights[^.]{0,160}\bfrom the 1920s to the 1940s|\bfrom the 1920s to the 1940s[^.]{0,80}Myrtle Heights|National Register[^.]{0,80}from the 1920s to the 1940s
struck: It is on the National Register of Historic Places for its houses from the 1920s to the 1940s.
use: Myrtle Heights is on the National Register for houses from 1925 to 1949 [NPS, NRIS 96001217].

pattern: keeps the city's last maritime forest|Ingram Dunes[^.]{0,120}\bkeeps\b
struck: Ingram Dunes Nature Preserve, on Hillside Drive at 9th Avenue South, keeps the city's last maritime forest.
use: Ingram Dunes Nature Preserve is the last remaining maritime forest in North Myrtle Beach, with native dunes 30 feet tall and an interpretive half-mile nature trail [nmb.us].

pattern: \btwo launch lanes\b|\bFrom the same lot, boardwalks
struck: It has two launch lanes, a floating dock and a fish cleaning station. From the same lot, boardwalks cross the marsh to Heritage Shores Nature Preserve.
use: The ramp has a two-lane boat launch, a kayak launch, a fishing pier, a floating boat dock and a fish cleaning station; the park gives access and parking for Heritage Shores Nature Preserve, an island in the marsh reached by elevated boardwalks (parking at the west end of 53rd Avenue North, about 4 blocks from the preserve entrance) [nmb.us].

pattern: \btree care ordinance\b|streets were laid out around
struck: Its streets were laid out around its live oaks, and the city has a tree care ordinance.
use: Conway's streets were designed around its live oaks [City of Conway news]. (Cut the ordinance: its text was not opened.)

pattern: Garden City Beach is a strip of land
struck: Garden City Beach is a strip of land between the ocean and the salt marsh of Murrells Inlet.
use: (cut it: the row cites OpenStreetMap, which the verifier did not open; keep the shore distance and the landing)

struck: Myrtle Heights is along Ocean Boulevard from about 32nd to 46th Avenue North.
use: The Myrtle Heights-Oak Park Historic District is along Ocean Boulevard from about 32nd to 46th Avenue North. Myrtle Heights is its southern part, from 32nd to 40th.

struck: Its houses built from 1925 to 1949 put it on the National Register of Historic Places.
use: The district's houses were built from about 1925 to 1945, and it is on the National Register of Historic Places [NRHP nomination, 1998].

pattern: \bbuilt in the Craftsman and Colonial Revival styles
struck: Those houses were built in the Craftsman and Colonial Revival styles.
use: The most common style is Colonial Revival, with some Bungalow and Craftsman touches [NRHP nomination, 1998].

struck: Two of the houses for sale are from that era, and a new oceanfront house was listed beside them.
use: (cut 'beside them': the new 2026 oceanfront house at 3604 N Ocean Blvd is about 160 m from the 1938 house and about 300 m from the 1946 house, which is on Kings Highway)

pattern: \$5\.8 million, the highest prices on this list
struck: Houses here were listed from about $750,000 to $5.8 million, the highest prices on this list.
use: Houses here were listed from about $750,000 to $5.8 million. The typical price, about $1.6 million, is the highest of the 16 areas.

pattern: \bthese are the lowest prices on this list
struck: At about $250,000, these are the lowest prices on this list.
use: At about $250,000, this is the lowest typical price on this list.

struck: The oceanfront Boardwalk begins at the 2nd Avenue Pier.
use: (cut it, or add a primary row for the Boardwalk's ends: the cited city page says only 'from pier to pier' and 'to 16th Avenue North')

pattern: \bOn Collins Street and Chester Street, the houses for sale were built in the 1950s and 1960s
struck: On Collins Street and Chester Street, the houses for sale were built in the 1950s and 1960s.
use: On Collins Street, Chester Street, Dunbar Street and 13th Avenue South, four houses for sale were built from 1955 to 1960.

struck: Nearby, a row of new houses was listed, also with no HOA dues.
use: On 12th Avenue South, 8 new houses in The Villages at Withers Heights were listed, also with no HOA fee.

pattern: \bolder houses within a mile and a half of the center
struck: Downtown Myrtle Beach, Conway and Loris: older houses within a mile and a half of the center.
use: Downtown Myrtle Beach (older streets and some new houses), Conway and Loris: houses within a mile and a half of the center.

pattern: \boutside a named subdivision has no homeowners association
struck: Almost every house on a street outside a named subdivision has no homeowners association (HOA) fee.
use: Almost every house listed on a street outside a named subdivision shows no homeowners association (HOA) fee.

pattern: \bPlantation Point pays HOA dues|\bolder Pine Lakes streets pays no HOA dues
struck: Not one house for sale in Plantation Point pays HOA dues.
use: Every house for sale in Plantation Point was listed with no HOA fee.

pattern: \bmost houses for sale come without an HOA fee
struck: Around Rosewood Drive in Socastee, most houses for sale come without an HOA fee.
use: Around Rosewood Drive in Socastee, most houses for sale are listed with no HOA fee.

pattern: \bAlmost every home for sale in Crescent Beach
struck: Almost every home for sale in Crescent Beach is listed with no HOA dues.
use: Nearly 9 in 10 homes for sale in Crescent Beach are listed with no HOA dues.

struck: 6. Crescent Beach: almost no HOA, and a maritime forest
use: 6. Crescent Beach: nearly 9 in 10 with no HOA fee, and a maritime forest

struck: On the ocean side of Surfside Beach, almost every home for sale is free of HOA dues.
use: On the ocean side of Surfside Beach, 6 in 7 homes for sale are listed with no HOA fee.

struck: Within a mile and a half of downtown Conway, almost every house for sale has no HOA fee.
use: Within a mile and a half of downtown Conway, 20 of 23 houses for sale are listed with no HOA fee.

struck: Age is the best sign.
use: Age is one sign: a house built before 1990 is far more likely to be listed with no HOA fee.

pattern: \bMyrtle Beach's first golf course|\bcity's first golf course
struck: These are the streets around Pine Lakes Country Club, Myrtle Beach's first golf course.
use: These are the streets around Pine Lakes Country Club, a golf course that opened in 1927.

struck: Canals were dug through the Cherry Grove marsh as early as the 1950s.
use: Cherry Grove's canals were created as early as the 1950s.

pattern: \bThe city dredges them\b|\bso owners on the canals can take a boat
struck: The city dredges them, so owners on the canals can take a boat to House Creek and the Intracoastal Waterway at high and low tide.
use: The city has dredged canals there twice since 2016, to give owners boat access to House Creek and the Intracoastal Waterway at high and low tide.

struck: Owners on the canals also pay the city about $1,700 a year for the dredging.
use: Owners of about 415 properties in the canal district pay the city about $1,700 a year for that work, on the county tax bill.

pattern: \bCherry Grove has canals to the inlet
struck: A boat at home. Cherry Grove has canals to the inlet.
use: Cherry Grove has canals with boat access to House Creek and the Intracoastal Waterway.

pattern: \bCity residents can register to park there free
struck: City residents can register to park there free.
use: North Myrtle Beach residents can register for free parking there, for a limited number of vehicles.

pattern: \bAlmost every Little River subdivision has an HOA|\balmost all of Little River's named subdivisions
struck: Almost every Little River subdivision has an HOA.
use: In Little River's named subdivisions, 179 of 192 homes for sale list an HOA fee.

struck: In the early 1920s, its boatmen began taking visitors fishing offshore, the first boats in South Carolina to do it for a fee.
use: In about the early 1920s, Little River's boatmen began taking visitors fishing for a fee, the first organized offshore trips of that kind in South Carolina.

struck: Since the inlet's jetties were built, boats can cross the bar at any time of day.
use: After the jetties were finished in 1983, boats could cross the inlet bar at any time of day.

pattern: \btwo oldest swing bridges on South Carolina
struck: It is one of the two oldest swing bridges on South Carolina's highways.
use: It is one of the two oldest of the seven swing-span highway bridges in the state's historic bridge inventory.

struck: Socastee Recreation Park has ball fields, a disc golf course, trails and a playground.
use: Socastee Recreation Park has multi-purpose fields, picnic areas, a disc-golf course, trails and a playground.

struck: The county's Stanley Drive boat landing is 5 minutes from the middle of Garden City.
use: The county's Stanley Drive boat landing is about 6 minutes from the middle of Garden City.

struck: 12. Garden City Beach: between the ocean and the marsh
use: (cut it: the row cites OpenStreetMap, which no verifier opened; head the entry with what the area gives a buyer)

struck: Flood insurance is the cost of the view: most houses here are in a high-risk flood zone, where a lender requires it.
use: Most houses here are in a high-risk flood zone, where with a mortgage your lender will almost always require flood insurance.

struck: You give up the beach next door: it is about 35 minutes by car, and Coastal Grand Mall about 50.
use: The beach is about 35 minutes by car, and Coastal Grand Mall about 50.

pattern: \bno public service picks up trash|\bwhich the county does not do outside the towns
struck: Outside the towns, no public service picks up trash at the curb.
use: Outside the towns, the Solid Waste Authority provides no curbside trash pickup.

struck: Its pavilion drew crowds to dance the shag, which South Carolina made its official state dance.
use: In the Ocean Drive and Crescent Beach area, a pavilion and amusement park drew crowds who danced the shag. South Carolina made the shag its official state dance in 1984.

pattern: \bEvery Thursday from June through September, the city holds
struck: Every Thursday from June through September, the city holds free Music on Main concerts at the Horseshoe on Main Street.
use: Each summer, the city holds free Music on Main concerts on Thursdays at the Horseshoe on Main Street, on a schedule the city sets.

pattern: \bOcean Drive Estates, houses from the mid-1980s were listed at about \$300,000
struck: In Ocean Drive Estates, houses from the mid-1980s were listed at about $300,000.
use: In Ocean Drive Estates, five houses from the mid-1980s were listed from $255,000 to $369,000.

pattern: \bNone of the houses for sale here would need flood insurance
struck: None of the houses for sale here would need flood insurance for a mortgage.
use: None of the 15 houses we placed on the county map would need flood insurance for a mortgage.

pattern: \bEach of those houses is half a mile or less from the ocean
struck: Each of those houses is half a mile or less from the ocean, on streets such as Hillside Drive.
use: Each of the 25 houses we placed on the county map is half a mile or less from the ocean, on streets such as Hillside Drive.

struck: The beach on foot. In Crescent Beach, Windy Hill, Ocean Drive, Myrtle Heights and Surfside Beach, most houses are within half a mile of the sand.
use: Near the beach. In Crescent Beach, Windy Hill, Ocean Drive, Myrtle Heights and Surfside Beach, most houses are within half a mile of the ocean shore, in a straight line.

struck: The trade-off is the beach: it is on the far side of Kings Highway, a 3.7-mile drive and too far to walk.
use: The trade-off is the beach: it is on the far side of Kings Highway, about 10 minutes away by car and too far to walk.

struck: Fuller Park, with tennis courts and a playground, is among those streets.
use: Fuller Park, with a playground, is about 0.1 mile from the middle of those streets.

pattern: \bone work van or pickup up to 21 feet long overnight
struck: The town allows two boats or trailers at a home, and one work van or pickup up to 21 feet long overnight.
use: The town allows two boats or trailers at a home, and one work van or pickup up to 21 feet long and 7 feet 11 inches high overnight.

pattern: \$34 a month on the utility bill
struck: Inside the city, the city picks up trash, recycling and yard waste at the curb once a week, for about $34 a month on the utility bill.
use: Inside the city, the city picks up trash, recycling and yard waste at the curb once a week, for $33.93 a month for a home.
